title: Baby Sunscreen Label Dataset (US, with EU and Australian limits)
description:
A weekly, reproducible dataset of US sunscreen drug labels from the FDA's DailyMed database (all sunscreen labels, about 14,000), with a week-by-week formulation history and the legal limits of 20 UV filters in the US (FDA OTC monograph M020 and final orders), the EU (Cosmetics Regulation Annex VI) and Australia (TGA Permissible Ingredients Determination), each value linked to its source.

For sunscreens labeled for babies or kids, each label's printed Drug Facts (text, or label images transcribed twice independently) is compared with the structured ingredient data the manufacturer filed with the FDA. The printed label decides. Published counts include: actives the FDA has proposed need more safety data; homosalate above the EU limit; synthetic SPF boosters and UV-filter stabilizers listed as inactive ingredients; fragrance, including fragrance printed on the label but absent from the FDA filing; parabens; isobutylparaben and methylisothiazolinone, which the EU no longer allows in leave-on cosmetics; oxybenzone and octinoxate (Hawaii); spray forms; labels whose Drug Facts match a label without baby or kids wording; front-panel 'mineral' wording on labels with organic UV filters; and 'hypoallergenic' labels that list fragrance. Every inclusion, exclusion and correction of a filing error is recorded with its reason and evidence.

A DailyMed listing is not proof that a product is on US shelves. Counts describe labels, not safety or market share.
